content: International Emergency Medicine is a specialized field that focuses on assessing the current standards and advancements in emergency medicine across various countries worldwide. In the United States, emergency medicine has been recognized as a distinct medical specialty for over two decades. The term International Emergency Medicine typically refers to the transfer of expertise and knowledge from well-established emergency medicine systems to those that are less developed. This includes the dissemination of knowledge related to ambulance operations and other critical components of emergency care systems. In many developing nations, efforts are underway to establish emergency medicine as a formal specialty, create accreditation mechanisms, and promote the development of training programs in this field. International Emergency Medicine (IEM) is considered a sub-specialty of emergency medicine. In the United States, there are several International Emergency Medicine Fellowship programs where residency-trained emergency physicians receive advanced training in international healthcare systems and skills development. These fellowship programs often include the opportunity to pursue an advanced degree in public health, such as a Master of Public Health (MPH). Fellowship programs in International Emergency Medicine are offered at several prestigious institutions, including: Alameda County Medical Center Highland Hospital Loma Linda University Keck School of Medicine at the University of Southern California George Washington University Emory University Medical College of Georgia Rush University / Cook County Hospital University of Illinois at Chicago The Johns Hopkins University University of Maryland Bellevue Hospital Center / New York University Columbia University / New York Presbyterian Hospital Long Island Jewish Medical Center University of Rochester Medical Center University of Pittsburgh Rhode Island Hospital Brown University The International Conference on Emergency Medicine (ICEM) is a biennial event organized by emergency physicians from around the world under the auspices of the International Federation for Emergency Medicine. This federation was originally established by four national emergency physician organizations: the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), the British Association for Emergency Medicine (BAEM), the Canadian Association of Emergency Physicians (CAEP), and the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM). Historically, the conference has rotated among the founding member organizations. However, in recent years, numerous new members have joined the federation, and the conference will now rotate among these new members as well.
